title: Thought, speech and action through the chain of descent
overview:
This stretch of the chapter follows one paradigm, thought (*machshava*), speech (*dibur*) and action (*maaseh*), through the whole chain of descent (*seder hishtalshelus*). Its first example is the end of the deed: the final deeds of our *avoda* arose in G-d's first thought, the cause of the whole chain. G-d's essential thought has the same three parts: the final deed, the speech of thought (letters engraved within the self, "He said and it came to be"), and the thought of thought, where an idea is plugged into words. The words "I will be king" (*Ana Emloch*) express the will and wisdom behind creation.

After the *tzimtzum* the pattern goes down again, through the *ratzon kadum*, *Adam Kadmon*, *Atik Yomin* and *Arich Anpin*. It also runs through a person, whose hidden thought descends to the feelings of the heart, called *Leah*; speech is *Rachel*. The large *dalet* of *Echad*, speech still joined to its source in thought, and *Zeir Anpin*'s ten *sefiros* show the same paradigm. The chapter closes with *Etz Chaim*: the heel of Leah enters the head of Rachel, humility is the heel and fear is the head, and action is proper only when the inner *kavana* is present.

sections.title: Every level has thought, speech and action, and the end of the deed comes first
sections.summary: The three levels of thought, speech and action appear at every stage of the chain of worlds. In G-d's essential thought, the final deed came first, and G-d knows the world as something that appears separate.

All the levels go back to their source, which arose in G-d's simple thought. The infinite light before the *tzimtzum* is G-d's self-expression, His revelation to Himself, and everything is an extension of it on the model of *machshava* and *dibur*.

The *machshava* of *machshava* arranges those symbols into words, which express an idea higher than the letters: intellect and emotion expressed in thought.

The *seder hishtalshelus* is a means to an end: G-d wanted something essential, and could have created the world in many other ways.
That He chose these ten *sefiros* and these worlds is all a *levush*. The plan behind it is the *dibur* of *machshava*, the engraving of letters within the self.

sections.title: I will be king: the will and wisdom behind creation, and the depth of G-d's thought
sections.summary: G-d's will to be King rests on His essential wisdom and will, and the chesed that awakened creation was stirred by our deeds. The depth of His thought is infinite, and our avoda reveals it.

The words "I will be king" rest on G-d's essential wisdom and will.

G-d envisioned our deeds, which triggered the *chafetz chesed*; it arose in His thought and will, and then the revelation of the powers. So our *avoda* reaches the arousal of the will.
Our *avoda* reaches the beginning of the thought, up to the cause of the entire *seder hishtalshelus*.

blocks.text: The depth of a thought is the depth of the idea behind it; so too G-d's essential thought in the essence of the infinite light.
This infinite wisdom and infinite will being expressed can never be fully investigated or expressed: every creature is a variation of this original thought.
We are separate from G-d and must do *avoda*: that perspective is the ultimate purpose of creation. So our *avoda* is serious, reaching to the very essence.

Through *avoda* we reveal G-d's infinitely deep essence, with no end to the new lights we can reveal. As he cites the *Hayom Yom*, the Baal Shem Tov compares the Jewish people to the ground, whose treasures only mining can reveal.

Thought corresponds to *Beriah*, speech to *Yetzirah* and action to *Asiyah*, as it says: "I created him, I formed him, and I even made him," for My honor.

blocks.title: A home you want to feel
blocks.text: Like wanting a home to feel a certain way in, versus what you do outside to get it.
Then we come to *Adam Kadmon*, where we create associations of what the essential desire will mean outside. As explained in chapters 18 and 19, those associations are creating a *machshava*.
The desire is filtered and condensed at each stage: *Adam Kadmon*, *Atik Yomin*, *Arich Anpin*.

*Adam Kadmon*'s *ratzon* is like a person creating a self-image and worldview that makes these associations. Here G-d sets up the basic logic of the Torah, of good and bad, of reality, time and space. Those systems are *Adam Kadmon*.
Then *ratzon* and *taanug* are revealed in *Atik* and *Arich*, making some things desirable: those that reveal G-dliness and those that hide it.
Each level has three stages: the essential thing (the *maaseh* of *machshava*), its symbol (*dibur*), and the *kavana* plugged into it (*machshava* of *machshava*), down to every detail.

blocks.title: The hidden thought in a person
blocks.text: In a person, the essential thought hidden in the soul becomes revealed in will, *sechel* and *middos*: a plan for a specific thing, and how he feels about it.
The thought that clothes the heart's feelings is called *Leah*.

blocks.title: Sensations and words
blocks.text: All three levels appear here too. When a person is happy, angry or sad, his heart rate and breathing change: that is the *maaseh* of *machshava*. He names the feeling, "I'm feeling happy." This helps teach children to identify feelings.
Then we attach a reason and theory for the feeling and what to do about it: the *machshava* of *machshava*, sometimes right, sometimes wrong.

Judgment works measure for measure, on what we do with Torah and mitzvos, as with the Flood before and after: Hashem spoke to His heart, whether to destroy the world. This is speech in thought.

Once a thought becomes a decree (*dibur*) and is expressed, it happens; but what we do can lead to a *midda* such as *din*, which can be changed.
The thought changes within *machshava*, so it never reaches *dibur* or *maaseh*.

blocks.title: The Flood and repentance
blocks.text: The Flood: had they done repentance, the waters would have become waters of blessing. He thinks it was because of Noach.
Noach could change, so for him the Flood was not devastating; for others it had its result.
G-d sets things up: His will, *sechel* and *middos* plug into a *machshava* and certain letters in an external form, and this causes external events.
What it means depends partly on us: negative if we stay as we are, good if we change. We can learn, change and grow, and that causes the change: measure for measure.

and this is enough to understand

blocks.text: As it says, the heart does not reveal itself to the mouth. G-d does not decree who will be a *tzaddik* and who a *rasha*; tendencies and situations make one or the other easier.
These are the opportunities, the *machshava* of *machshava*; what it means for the person depends on his choice.
Some people turn a difficult start around to good. We can change how a thought goes from *machshava* to *dibur*.

blocks.title: The fractal
blocks.text: A pattern repeats: zoomed out, a thing shows a structure, and zoomed in, the same structure appears again, in the whole *seder hishtalshelus* and in every detail.

*Adam Kadmon* is *machshava*, the level of *Adam d'Beriah*. *Atik* and *Arich*, the revealed will in a specific thing, are like *dibur*, the *Adam d'Yetzirah*; *Zeir Anpin* is *maaseh*, the *Adam d'Asiyah*.

*Adam Kadmon* creates associations, the initial language out of content. What is chosen to express, the *dibur*, is the revealed will and *taanug* of *Atik* and *Arich*; what is done is the effect, the *middos* of *Zeir Anpin*.
This explains how the Torah and its laws are created, and specific providence in running the world, in many aspects of the *seder hishtalshelus*.

to somebody that understands these things
based on what we've explained

phrases.he: מכמה ריבוי פרטים מבחינת מעשה דמחשבה העצמית בעצמות אור אין סוף עד בחינת עשיה שבמחשבה דזעיר אנפין דאצילות
phrases.en: you can understand many, many details of the *seder hishtalshelus*

blocks.text: Understood in general and particulars, from the infinite light to the *asiya* of thought of *Zeir Anpin*.
This relationship lets you understand many details of the *seder hishtalshelus*.
A text such as *Etz Chaim* can be understood with this, from before the *tzimtzum* down to the thought of *Zeir Anpin*, and into the actual worlds.

phrases.he: וזה שנאמר כל אשר חפץ יהו״ה,
phrases.en: and this is what it says

phrases.he: במחשבה העצמית, עשה מאין דאצילות לבריאה כו׳)
phrases.en: that the relationship of a *machshava* is that G-d is taking something that's abstract, like a *sechel* and a *ratzon*, and you're creating symbols to represent that

blocks.text: G-d takes what is abstract, like *sechel* and *ratzon*, and creates symbols to represent it: the idea of words and of creating associations.
From Hashem's essential *ratzon* down to *Atzilus* going into *Beriah*.
At every layer, the essential g-dly thing creates a *levush*, a symbol that connects and reveals it. It is not necessary; it is G-d's choice to make those connections.
Although it all fits together and we think this is simply how things work, at every layer the connections are created, and they are not essential.

sections.title: The large dalet of Echad: Zeir Anpin's unity of the ten sefiros
sections.summary: Echad is Zeir Anpin, whose letters and ten sefiros express the unity of Atzilus, and the dalet is the source of Malchus, speech still joined to its source in thought.

phrases.en: we can understand this relationship also
this is the idea of the large *dalet* of the word *Echad*, which is the idea of the source of *dibur*, the way it is in the self before it comes out

blocks.text: We understand this relationship in the large *dalet* of *Echad*: the source of *dibur*, before it comes out.

phrases.en: this is the idea of *Malchus of tevuna*
which is the external level of understanding of *bina*

phrases.he: כו', והוא ענין קשר של תפילין של ראש
phrases.en: and this is represented also by the knot, the dalet on the back of the knot of the head *tefillin*

blocks.text: Malchus of tevuna, the external level of bina, the back of Ima: the source of associations, as in chapter 2.
The source creates the language; the knot of the head *tefillin* represents it, its dalet on the back.

phrases.he: הרי יובן דרך פרט בבחינת זעיר אנפין שנקרא אחד בבחינת אחדות דעשר ספירות דאצילות
phrases.en: so we can understand this relationship in a more specific way, of how this is that *Zeir Anpin* is called *Echad*
and in the general worlds we'd call this *Adam d'Asiyah*, but in the specific worlds we call this *Atzilus*

blocks.text: *Zeir Anpin* is called *Echad*, the unity of the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus*.
The *aleph* of *Echad* is *chachma*; the *ches*, seven middos, *bina* and seven middos again; the *dalet*, the four corners of *Malchus*: the unity of the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus*.
Generally, *Adam d'Asiyah*; in specific worlds, *Atzilus*.

phrases.en: this is the source for the thought that's called *Leah*
which is coming in a certain idea of *osios* and certain orders
and this is called the thought of thought

blocks.text: The source of the thought called *Leah*, which expresses the middos: the inner logic behind the reasons for the mitzvos, which the Gemara gives as human intellect. That is in *Beriah*; its source is why certain things are G-dly.

Similarly, in running the world: the logic of how it works, the laws of nature, or what the Rebbe liked to call laws of creation. Symbols, letters and associations change meaning with the order they come in.
Thought of thought, from *Malchus of tevuna*: the inner *kavana* that plugs in and creates these systems.
G-d's inner plan, the *kavana* of the Torah, the mitzvos and how the world is set up, is the thought of thought.

sections.title: The large dalet is speech still joined to thought; the hidden of all hidden
sections.summary: The large dalet is the source of speech in the self, and the thought behind it reaches up to the hidden of all hidden, which no thought can grasp.

phrases.en: and it's called a large *dalet*
which is the more mature level of speech

phrases.he: להיות מבואר למעלה שיש ב' מדריגות בזה
phrases.en: like we explained there's two levels within this

blocks.text: The *dalet rabasi* is the greater maturity of speech; there are two levels within it, as explained above.
The large *dalet* is language still connected to its source within the self.

phrases.en: and really this is also called *dibur* of *machshava*
because you think the idea in different words
even if you're not planning on speaking it

blocks.text: Coming up with words yourself, from your own real thoughts, is a real new idea: the large *dalet*, from *Malchus of tevuna*. Hearing others' words is different.
This too is *dibur* of *machshava*: thinking the idea in words, even if you won't speak it.
There is an overlap: you first think the idea to yourself; then, once you create words and symbols for it, you can use them to tell someone else.

phrases.en: and this is the large *dalet* of *Echad*
The *aleph* and *ches* are the nine *sefiros*, one plus eight, of *Echad*
and then the *dalet* represents the *Malchus* of *Zeir Anpin*

phrases.he: כו' שכל מדה וספירה באה באותיות וצירופים דמחשבה דלאה
phrases.en: that every single *middah* and every single *sefira*, G-d chooses certain ways of expressing it

phrases.he: כו' מכח ושרש המחשבה בחינת מלכות דתבונה כו'
phrases.en: and this comes from the source and the root of thought, which is *Malchus of tevuna*

blocks.text: *Aleph* and *ches* make nine by gematria: the nine *sefiros* of *Zeir Anpin*.
The *dalet* is their *Malchus*. Every *middah* and *sefira* comes in letters of *Leah*'s thought, and G-d chooses how each is expressed.
Take creation from nothing, the *middah* of *chesed*: G-d chose one of infinite ways, and that choice is the letters of the thought.
From *Malchus of tevuna*, the source of thought: the ability to create associations and symbols, G-d's choice how to set it up.

phrases.en: and this is why it says when we say *Shema*, we have to elongate the *dalet* of *Echad* when we're contemplating G-d's unity

phrases.he: להיותו שרש בחינת המלכות בד' סטרי עלמא
phrases.en: because it's the source of *Malchus* across the four corners of the world

phrases.he: שביחודא תתאה דברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד כו')

blocks.text: Elongating the *dalet* of *Echad* in the *Shema* contemplates G-d's unity: the source of *Malchus* across the four corners, the lower unity of *Baruch shem kvod malchuso*.
The diverse things we see are the way they are because G-d chose to create the system so; so they express His will and wisdom.
Time, space and the laws of creation need not be as they are: a purposeful system set up by His choice, so it expresses something of Him.

phrases.he: וגם הנה מובן דרך כללות, במחשבה הקדומה עד במחשבה הפשוטה דאחדות הפשוטה בעצמותו ממש,
phrases.en: And similarly, we can also zoom out and look at how this relationship is in the highest, most general levels, going back to the general thought, the *machshava kduma* of the *ratzon kadum*, all the way back before the *tzimtzum* to the simple thought of the simple unity in the essence
which is called the hidden of all hidden things
that no thought can grasp Him
even the thought of *Adam Kadmon*, all those *ratzon*, the *ratzon* associations are created

phrases.he: כו', דדלי"ת רבתי הוא כשעלה באותיות מחשבתו ורצונו הפשוט
phrases.en: then the *dalet* would be the letters of Hashem's thought, expressing His the way it's included in the *ratzon*, His *ratzon* before the *tzimtzum*

phrases.he: כו', שהוא בא מבחינת מלכות דתבונתו העצמית כו' ודי למבין
phrases.en: that those that essential *machshava* also comes from *Malchus of tevuna* of the essence, and so there's that similar kind of relationship

blocks.text: Zooming out to the highest levels: from the general thought, the *machshava kduma* of the *ratzon kadum*, back before the *tzimtzum* to the simple unity in His essence.
This is the *stima d'chol stimin*, the hidden of all hidden: no thought can grasp Him. Even the whole concept of the ten *sefiros* is something G-d created, so His essence transcends it.
Just as *Malchus* creating the worlds need not be as it is, so the highest things we take for granted are not necessary: they are a language created for Him to express Himself.
Even the *Adam Kadmon* associations and the logic of the Torah are created. We do it because Hashem wants it, and part of what He wants is that it have this reason and logic.

With the large *dalet* of *Echad*, the *dalet* is the letters of Hashem's simple will, as included in His *ratzon* before the *tzimtzum*: a creative process by G-d behind the systems and symbols we have.
This can be seen in *Atzilus* and back to the beginning of the *seder hishtalshelus* on every level. Essential thought also comes from *Malchus of tevuna* of the essence.

sections.title: Leah and Rachel: humility as the heel, fear as the head
sections.summary: The heel of Leah is humility, which is hidden thought, and the head of Rachel is fear, which is revealed speech. Action is proper only when the inner kavana is present.

phrases.en: this that it says in *Etz Chaim*

phrases.he: דעקבי לאה נכנסין תוך ראש רחל
phrases.en: the heels of *Leah* enter the head of *Rachel*

phrases.he: כו', וכמאר רבותינו זכרונם לברכה מה שעשתה ענוה עקב לסוליתא
phrases.en: and this is what our sages say, that what humility made a shoe for her foot
fear made a crown for her head

phrases.he: כו', היינו בחינת דבור שבמחשבה שנעשית מחשבה שבדבור
phrases.en: this is the idea how the words of thought become the thought of the words
and this is the idea that the heel of humility

blocks.text: To round off, the *Etz Chaim* says the heels of Leah enter the head of Rachel: a relationship of thought to speech.

The *Etz Chaim* describes the main *partzufim* (*Atik*, *Arich*, *Abba*, *Ima*, *Zeir Anpin*, *Nukva*) and more with specific roles. Leah focuses on thought as a garment for the middos; Rachel on speech.
These two garments are of *Zeir Anpin*: *Yaakov*, *Yisroel*, Rachel and Leah.
Our sages: humility made a shoe for her foot, and fear made a crown for her head.
The inner dimension of Torah is the hidden reason behind things; the revealed Torah is the outer part. So the lowest level of Leah becomes the highest of Rachel.
What one understands of the inner *kavana*, its *Malchus*, becomes the inner *keser* of revealed Torah.
The *dibur* of *machshava* becomes the *machshava* of *dibur*.
On a revealed level, the reasons in the *Shulchan Aruch* or the Gemara come from a deeper understanding, hidden even in Chazal and the midrash.
All the secrets of Torah are hidden in *Ein Yaakov*; understand things on different levels.

blocks.title: A child's effort
blocks.text: Like telling a child the point is their effort: they are really growing and learning.
The deeper, the teacher's, perspective: there is always an inner and an outer, humility and fear.

The *Sefer HaChinuch* and the *Rambam* explain the reasons for mitzvos. Many are done out of fear because Hashem said so, but many teach humility, kindness and flexibility. He thinks this is related too.
Thought is hidden: that is the heel of humility.

phrases.en: because *machshava*, something that's hidden, it's kept to oneself, and I guess that's the idea of humility, that there's certain *bittul* there that's not revealed
that it's something that's more abstract, and it's transcendent, and can't be expressed
but the speech is what can be revealed and can be expressed
and so therefore it's something that's a *yesh*, it has a certain *gaavah* or arrogance to it, so to speak, because it's very tangible

phrases.he: כו', ונעשית עטרה וכתר לרחל בחינת הדבור
phrases.en: and that becomes the crown for *Rachel*, the level of *dibur*

blocks.text: Hidden thought (*ayin*) has a *bittul* that is not revealed; it is abstract, and deeper ideas cannot be explained. He guesses this is humility.
Speech is revealed and expressible: *yesh*, with a certain pride or arrogance, so to speak, because it is tangible.
Speech becomes Rachel's crown, *keser*.

phrases.he: כי בחינת כח ושרש וראש לדבור
phrases.en: what is the inner source and root and head for speech
it comes from those letters of thought
a person lose their train of thought, if they don't, if they stop thinking they're not going to be able to speak

blocks.text: Speech's inner strength, root and head are the letter combinations of thought.
Simply: no language to think in and no thinking, so nothing to say.
If the train of thought stops, speech stops, as is known.

phrases.he: וזה שכתוב עקב ענוה יראת יהו״ה
phrases.en: following humility comes the fear of G-d
as it is explained elsewhere

blocks.text: Following humility comes the fear of G-d. Without the inner *kavana*, the connection to Hashem, a person will not express it externally through the fear of G-d.
As it is explained elsewhere: learning the inner dimension of Torah and being aware of what we do matters, since without that *kavana* a person cannot act properly in the small details.

reviewQuestions.question: What is the end of the deed that comes first, and where is it in G-d's essential thought?
What are the three levels of thought, and how does thought of thought differ from them?
How does the large dalet of Echad express speech in the self?
How do Leah and Rachel relate to thought and speech, and what does Etz Chaim say of them?
What does the class say awakened the desire for kindness that created the world?
